title: Jackson School and music in school
summary: He went to Jackson School c. 1905 with future musicians in the school orchestra; music taught briefly by blackboard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Oh, well, there was practically no trouble. Once in a while, one out of a hundred might decide to crack a Chinaman's windowpane or something, you know, something like that. But, uh, as a rule, I'd say 99 percent of the kids were kids. They didn't, uh, well, they were taught better. There wasn't any reason to go around and throw rocks at the feet. Where'd you go to school, uh, um? I went to Jackson School. Did you? Toxico Magazine. Uh-huh. How far'd you go in school? I went to Top. And I went, uh, when I went there, we had an orchestra, school orchestra. And fellas like Gussie Miller, Eddie Edwards, they were in it. Ellie Coulon, he was in it. I have to laugh when those guys tell me how young they are, you know?
What year was that? Do you remember?
Oh, Lord, let's see. That would be about, uh...

No. That'd be about, uh, 1905, I guess. Something like that. Of course, you see, the first day I had, my, I was taught at home by my sisters. Oh, they did? Give me a fortune. First day I went to school, I went to third grade. Ah. And the third grade was a lot more severe in those days than it is today. Ah. In other words, my comparison with the teaching today would be about, uh, third grade would be equivalent to fifth. Mm-hmm. And they had that split season deal.
They didn't teach music in the schools, though, did they?

Well, oh, yes. Not like today, no. They didn't give much time, about 15 minutes, but, uh, all of that training, that music training, was, uh, by a music teacher with a blackboard and notes. Mm-hmm. On the backboard.
